extracted.intended_audience: independent documentary filmmakers applying to the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/assessment criteria for submitting a proposal to the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund, including required materials, project readiness, evaluation criteria, and contract/reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sundance Institute Documentary Fund accepts submissions through periodic open calls. The next call for submissions will open on June 10, 2024 and close on July 15, 2024, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filmmakers who submit applications by then will be notified regarding the status of their application in early 2025. Do not expect extensions (see 'No').

rubrics_metrics.name: No deadline extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you offer deadline extensions? No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must meet published open-call deadlines; late submissions will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: How long do your decisions take? Decisions typically take six to eight months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not contact staff for status updates; applicants will be notified directly by email once a decision has been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project phase and readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your film only when you have written or visual material that demonstrates your creative and storytelling intent. You may submit at any production phase from development through post-production. All proposals must convey some vision for a finished film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should have secured characters or subjects, be able to articulate a story or structure, and be able to explain the project's driving central question. The Fund is unable to consider proposals for story research. Applicants are encouraged to apply at least eight months before an anticipated premiere. Picture-locked cuts are ineligible for post-production funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic criteria (vision, voice, connection)
rubrics_metrics.description: We support cinematic documentaries embracing a wide range of aesthetic traditions and storytelling approaches and artists who demonstrate a clarity of vision, distinct voice, and meaningful connection to the story being told.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Documentary Fund spotlights new voices and artists bringing a fresh perspective to vital conversations of our day, often through new creative frontiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded film types
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not fund NGO, advocacy, or educational films, or branded content. We also tend not to fund purely historical or biographical films unless they show clear contemporary relevance or innovation in form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also explicitly excluded elsewhere: fiction films, short films, series, NGO films, advocacy films, educational films, and branded content. Short films may be funded via separate Documentary Short Fund calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and materials requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Films may be in any language, but we ask that proposals are written in English and that visual materials be subtitled in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgets must be translated into U.S. dollars. Visual samples and written proposals should be accessible to English-language reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The DFP prioritizes films with budgets under $1 million USD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should indicate total budget in USD; the Fund gives priority to lower-budget independent productions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative and editorial control
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative and editorial control must be held by members of the films’ key creative teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund supports projects led by the creative team (e.g., director) rather than externally controlled productions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority for historically underrepresented artists and regions
rubrics_metrics.description: In our funding we continue to uplift productions led by artists from communities that have been traditionally marginalized (e.g., artists who identify as BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and people with disabilities)... Our current international priorities are artists living and working in regions that lack a robust infrastructure of support for independent film, regions of conflict, and countries where freedom of expression is under threat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund seeks to unearth historically underrepresented narratives and elevate voices beyond borders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-length requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sundance Institute Documentary Fund supports projects that are feature-length documentaries (52 minutes and longer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid/animated and experimental documentaries are eligible; stand-alone short films are not funded by this Fund (see Documentary Short Fund).

rubrics_metrics.name: No completion-only funding / ineligible costs
rubrics_metrics.description: My project is finished. Can I apply for funding to pay for film transfers or reimburse debt, etc.? No. Film transfers, film prints, and debt reimbursement to complete work are not eligible for funding. We generally do not provide solely completion funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund aims to support creative and production processes rather than retroactive debt/transfer costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior funding not required but fundraising strategy required
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not have any funds secured to date. Am I still eligible for funding? Yes. Prior funding commitments are not required. Your written proposal should include a fundraising strategy for raising your film budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fundraising strategy should clearly distinguish between funds you have applied for and funds you have already secured. Examples include foundations, broadcast license agreements, private donations, in-kind support, crowdfunding, producer investment, and fundraisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive budget requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If I am applying for development funds, can my submitted budget cover the development portion of the project only? No. A budget covering the costs of the entire project from development through distribution is required for every funding category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a one- to two-page comprehensive line-item budget in U.S. dollars. Sample PDF and Excel templates are provided but may be tailored; you may use your own format as long as it provides the costs of the entire project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of impact / audience engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: What is meant by 'impact'? Audience engagement is a strategic campaign to encourage individuals and communities to move from passive to active participants on the issue your film broaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement campaigns are distinct from distribution (puts films on screens) and from marketing and outreach (gets viewers to see films). Rather, engagement is designed to activate audiences and stakeholders toward a specific goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual sample competitiveness and minimum lengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Development applicants are encouraged (but not required) to include a visual sample of up to 15 minutes in length... A minimum of 10 minutes of edited footage is required for production applications and 20 minutes of edited footage for post-production applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production or post-production proposals with very short reels (or with only trailers, teasers, or brief selects) are not competitive against the longer samples and rough cuts being submitted. The Sundance Institute guarantees watching up to 30 minutes of visual material provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous completed work sample rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed previous work may be any length from short to feature... If you have multiple previous works or several co-directors, please select one previous work that best reflects the vision for your new project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will not review more than one previous work sample. A previous work from a different member of the team (e.g., producer, editor, cinematographer) will not be considered as the director's prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted delivery formats for visual material
rubrics_metrics.description: We only accept samples via online streaming links. You must provide an online streaming link and password, if applicable, to your current rough cut or sample and to your completed previous work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend Vimeo or YouTube. Your film should be available for at least eight months after you submit. Do not update or change your uploaded file or its password once you submit. If we do not have the correct password, we will not be able to evaluate your project. We do not accept WeTransfer, Dropbox, Google Drive, or other such file-transfer services. DVDs are not accepted unless you request a DVD exemption due to significant impediments to internet access (email dfp@sundance.org).

rubrics_metrics.name: First-time director visual-sample guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A visual sample that conveys the director’s creative perspective and ability to execute is preferred. If this is a directorial debut, you may submit a film you have shot or edited instead, or you may choose not to submit a previous work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit previous work by another team member as if it were the director's work; such samples from different members will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete applications not reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Incomplete applications will not be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required written proposal fields, budget, and visual materials are provided in the online application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria used by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated on several criteria, including strong artistic vision, compelling storytelling, contemporary cultural relevance, originality, feasibility, journalistic rigor (where applicable), and potential to reach and connect with an intended audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fund also takes into consideration film teams’ access to resources (financial and creative) to ensure funds are prioritized for those who need them most. The creative team's connection to and engagement with the community they are working with is also considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: May I reapply for a grant if my proposal is declined? Yes. However, you may only reapply when your project has advanced considerably in storytelling vision and intent, preferably at a later stage of production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We discourage more than three applications to the Documentary Fund over the life of a project. Filmmakers are strongly discouraged from resubmitting nearly identical proposals or visual samples. If you reapply you must submit a complete, brand-new application with new video links and demonstrate significant development since the last application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple submissions allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I submit more than one proposal? Yes, you are allowed to submit more than one proposal in the same round as long as they are for separate projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each project must have its own complete application and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award terms (rights, reporting, and obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are not recoupable, and none of your exploitable rights are encumbered... To distribute funds, we require director and producer agreements as well as a clear chain of title to be in place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant agreement requires logo acknowledgment in the end credits and on promotional materials, a high-resolution digital copy of the film, narrative, financial, and distribution reports — and social impact reports, if applicable. Sundance may request active participation in the Institute creative community via invitation-only activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee distribution and festival independence
rubrics_metrics.description: If I receive a grant from Sundance Institute Documentary Fund, will my film screen at the Sundance Film Festival? No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees are encouraged to submit their completed work for Festival consideration directly to the Sundance Film Festival staff, which selects films independently. Receiving a grant does not encumber broadcast, theatrical, or DVD distribution rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback and inquiry limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If my project is declined, will staff provide feedback? Unfortunately, we have a limited staff and are unable to provide feedback to all applicants. However, projects that reach our final stage of review are eligible to receive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not call to discuss your film; Sundance does not respond to application-process inquiries via phone. If you still have specific questions after reading the FAQ, email dfp@sundance.org. Do not contact staff for status updates; they cannot provide them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application confirmation and availability guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: After you press 'submit' on the online application, a confirmation page will appear. You should also receive a confirmation email once your application is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have not received an email, please double-check your spam filter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical delivery support and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: What format should I submit my visual material in? We only accept samples via online streaming links... We recommend using Vimeo or YouTube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you live in a country with significant impediments to internet access, you may email dfp@sundance.org to request a DVD exemption. Also check provided links for PDF file-size reduction and Vimeo upload help.
